nodes.summary: On all nodes, `ancProd` is the joint.
nodes.title: The ancestral product on all nodes is the joint

nodes.summary: The product of the tables of the nodes in `A`, with the uniform distribution on the other nodes. For an ancestral `A` it has the same marginals on `A` as the joint (`marginal_joint_eq_ancProd`).
nodes.title: Product of the tables of an ancestral set

nodes.summary: A Bayesian network with values in a type $\alpha$ on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$, listed in a topological order, assigns to each node $k$ a finite set of parents among the earlier nodes $0, \dots, k - 1$, and a conditional probability table: for each assignment of values in $\alpha$ to the parents of $k$, a finitely supported probability distribution on $\alpha$ for the value of node $k$.
nodes.title: Bayesian network

nodes.summary: A chain of conditional distributions with values in a type $\alpha$ assigns to every $k \in \mathbb{N}$ and every assignment $(x_0, \dots, x_{k-1})$ of values in $\alpha$ to the variables $0, \dots, k - 1$ a finitely supported probability distribution $p_k(\cdot \mid x_0, \dots, x_{k-1})$ on $\alpha$, the conditional distribution of variable $k$ given the earlier ones.
nodes.title: Chain of conditional distributions

nodes.summary: Let $B$ be a Bayesian network on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$ with values in a nonempty type $\alpha$, and let $P_m$ be the joint distribution of the first $m$ nodes of $B$ viewed as a chain of conditional distributions. For a node $k < n$, write $p_k(\cdot \mid z)$ for its conditional probability table at values $z$ of its parents. Let $y = (y_0, \dots, y_{k-1}) \in \alpha^k$ with $P_k(y) \ne 0$, and write…
nodes.title: The ordered Markov property

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a chain of conditional distributions with values in a type $\alpha$, let $P_m$ be its joint distribution of the first $m$ variables, and let $p_n(\cdot \mid y)$ be its conditional distribution of variable $n$ given values $y \in \alpha^n$ of the earlier ones. For every $n$, every $y \in \alpha^n$ with $P_n(y) \ne 0$ and every $a \in \alpha$, we have $P_{n+1}(y, a) / P_n(y) = p_n(a \mid y)$, where…
nodes.title: Conditionals of the joint of a chain

nodes.summary: `FiniteWeight.CondIndep` for `Finset`s of nodes, with the unions taken in `Finset`.
nodes.title: Conditional independence for finite sets of nodes

nodes.summary: If `X ⫫ Y | Z` then `X' ⫫ Y | Z` for `X' ⊆ X`.
nodes.title: Decomposition

nodes.summary: The global Markov property for `Finset`s of nodes; `condIndep_of_dSeparated` is the statement for arbitrary sets of nodes.
nodes.title: Global Markov property for finite sets of nodes

nodes.summary: The global Markov property (soundness of d-separation: Geiger, Verma & Pearl 1990; Lauritzen, Dawid, Larsen & Leimer 1990): if `Z` d-separates `X` from `Y` in the graph of a Bayesian network, then `X` and `Y` are conditionally independent given `Z` under its joint law. No disjointness of `X`, `Y`, `Z` is needed.
nodes.title: The global Markov property

nodes.summary: Conditional independence is symmetric.
nodes.title: Symmetry of conditional independence

nodes.summary: If `X ∪ W ⫫ Y | Z` then `X ⫫ Y | Z ∪ W` (for a nonnegative law).
nodes.title: Weak union

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite nonempty type and $n \in \mathbb{N}$. For every function $P : \alpha^n \to \mathbb{R}$ with $P(x) \ge 0$ for all $x$ and $\sum_x P(x) = 1$, there is a chain of conditional distributions with values in $\alpha$ whose joint distribution of the first $n$ variables equals $P$.
nodes.title: The chain rule

nodes.summary: A set of nodes is ancestral if it contains the parents of each of its nodes.
nodes.title: Ancestral set of nodes

nodes.summary: Let $B$ be a Bayesian network on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$ with values in a nonempty type $\alpha$. The joint distribution of $B$ is the function $P : \alpha^n \to \mathbb{R}$ given by $P(x) = P_n(x)$ for $x \in \alpha^n$, where $P_n$ is the joint distribution of the first $n$ variables of the chain of conditional distributions of $B$.
nodes.title: Joint distribution of a Bayesian network

nodes.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. If two chains of conditional distributions $c$ and $c'$ with values in a type $\alpha$ have the same conditional distribution of variable $k$ given the earlier variables for every $k < n$, then they have the same joint distribution of the first $n$ variables.
nodes.title: Joint distribution determined by the first conditionals

nodes.summary: The joint is the product over nodes of the probability of the node's value given the values of its parents.
nodes.title: Factorization of a Bayesian network

nodes.summary: For a chain of conditional distributions with values in a type $\alpha$, write $p_k(\cdot \mid x_0, \dots, x_{k-1})$ for the conditional distribution of variable $k$ given the earlier ones and $P_n$ for the joint distribution of the first $n$ variables. Then for every $n$ and every $x \in \alpha^n$ we have $P_n(x) = \prod_{k < n} p_k(x_k \mid x_0, \dots, x_{k-1})$.
nodes.title: Factorization of the joint of a chain

nodes.summary: For a chain of conditional distributions with values in a type $\alpha$, write $p_k(\cdot \mid x_0, \dots, x_{k-1})$ for the conditional distribution of variable $k$ given the earlier ones. The joint distribution $P_n : \alpha^n \to \mathbb{R}$ of the first $n$ variables is defined by the chain rule: $P_0 = 1$ and $P_{n+1}(x_0, \dots, x_n) = P_n(x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}) \, p_n(x_n \mid x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$.
nodes.title: Joint distribution of a chain

nodes.summary: `FiniteWeight.marginal` on a `Finset` of nodes, as a sum over a decidable filter.
nodes.title: Marginal on a finite set of nodes as a filtered sum

nodes.summary: `marginal P S x'` depends only on the values of `x'` on `S`.
nodes.title: A marginal depends only on the fixed variables

nodes.summary: Summing out one more variable `i ∉ S`.
nodes.title: Summing out one more variable from a marginal

nodes.summary: For an ancestral set `A` and `S ⊆ A`, the marginals of the joint on `S` are those of `ancProd A`.
nodes.title: The law of an ancestral set depends only on its tables

nodes.summary: Fixing more variables decreases the probability.
nodes.title: Fixing more variables decreases the marginal

nodes.summary: Let $B$ be a Bayesian network on the nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$ with values in a finite nonempty type $\alpha$, and let $P$ be its joint distribution. Then $\sum_{x \in \alpha^n} P(x) = 1$.
nodes.title: The joint distribution of a Bayesian network sums to one

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a chain of conditional distributions with values in a finite type $\alpha$, and write $P_k$ for its joint distribution of the first $k$ variables. For every $n$ and every $y = (y_0, \dots, y_{n-1}) \in \alpha^n$, $\sum_{a \in \alpha} P_{n+1}(y_0, \dots, y_{n-1}, a) = P_n(y)$.
nodes.title: Marginalizing the last variable of a chain

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a chain of conditional distributions with values in a finite type $\alpha$, and write $P_n$ for its joint distribution of the first $n$ variables. For every $n$, $\sum_{x \in \alpha^n} P_n(x) = 1$.
nodes.title: The joint distribution of a chain sums to one

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type, $M$ an additive commutative monoid, $n$ a natural number and $f : \alpha^{n+1} \to M$. Then $\sum_{x \in \alpha^{n+1}} f(x) = \sum_{y \in \alpha^n} \sum_{a \in \alpha} f(y_0, \dots, y_{n-1}, a)$, where $y = (y_0, \dots, y_{n-1})$.
nodes.title: Splitting a sum over $\alpha^{n+1}$ at the last coordinate

nodes.summary: A Bayesian network $b$ on nodes $0, \dots, n - 1$ with values in a nonempty type $\alpha$ defines a chain of conditional distributions. For $k < n$, the conditional distribution of variable $k$ given values $y_0, \dots, y_{k-1}$ of the earlier variables is the table of node $k$ applied to the values $y_j$ of its parents $j$. For $k \ge n$ it is the point mass at a fixed arbitrary element of $\alpha$.
nodes.title: The chain of a Bayesian network

nodes.summary: Given a chain $c$ of conditional distributions with values in $\alpha$, an index $n$ and a family $f$ assigning to each $y \in \alpha^n$ a probability distribution $f(y)$ on $\alpha$, the updated chain has conditional distribution $f$ for variable $n$ and the same conditional distribution as $c$ for every other variable.
nodes.title: Replacing one conditional of a chain

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
